---
title: "Parallel chains via Web Workers"
format: live-html
pyodide:
  packages:
    - micropip
---

`sampling()` runs one chain inside the page's own Pyodide kernel worker -- a single thread.
`StanModel.sampling_parallel(n_chains=...)` instead spawns one plain-JS Web Worker per chain (no Pyodide
in them, just [stanwasm](https://github.com/habakan/stanwasm)'s wasm module loaded fresh in each), so
multiple chains can run at once across whatever cores the browser gives them. Quarto Live's own Pyodide
runs in a dedicated Web Worker too (confirmed the same way as the [JupyterLite](../)/[marimo](../marimo/)
demos), so the Workers `sampling_parallel` spawns here aren't nested inside another Worker -- an easier
case, same as the [PyScript](../pyscript/) demo.

This needs nested-Worker support (a Worker spawning another Worker): current Chrome/Edge/Firefox, and
Safari 16.4+ (March 2023). Where that's unavailable it falls back to running the chains one at a time
through `sampling()` and prints a warning -- it never just fails.

Everything runs in a single block -- see [`linear-regression.qmd`](linear-regression.html) for why.

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: true
import json
import time
import micropip
from pyodide.code import run_js

site_base = run_js(
    """
    (() => {
      const href = self.location.href;
      const quarto = href.match(/^(.*)\\/[^\\/]+_files\\/libs\\/quarto-contrib\\//);
      if (quarto) return quarto[1];
      const markers = ["/extensions/", "/assets/"];
      for (const marker of markers) {
        const idx = href.indexOf(marker);
        if (idx !== -1) return href.slice(0, idx);
      }
      return self.location.origin;
    })()
    """
)

wheel_url = site_base + "/pystanwasm-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl"
await micropip.install(wheel_url)

import numpy as np
import pystanwasm as stan

print("pystanwasm", stan.__version__)

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
N, K = 500, 10
X = rng.normal(size=(N, K))
beta_true = rng.normal(0, 2, size=K)
alpha_true, sigma_true = 1.5, 1.2
y = alpha_true + X @ beta_true + rng.normal(0, sigma_true, size=N)

stan_code = """
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=0> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;
  vector[N] y;
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  vector[K] beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
  alpha ~ normal(0, 5);
  beta ~ normal(0, 5);
  sigma ~ exponential(1);
  y ~ normal(alpha + X * beta, sigma);
}
"""
data = {"N": N, "K": K, "X": X.tolist(), "y": y.tolist()}
N_CHAINS = 4

model = stan.StanModel(stan_code, stanwasm_path="/stanwasm/pkg/stanwasm.js")

t0 = time.perf_counter()
sequential_fits = [
    await model.sampling(data=data, iter=2000, warmup=1000, seed=42 + i)
    for i in range(N_CHAINS)
]
sequential_time = time.perf_counter() - t0

t1 = time.perf_counter()
parallel_fits = await model.sampling_parallel(data=data, n_chains=N_CHAINS, iter=2000, warmup=1000)
parallel_time = time.perf_counter() - t1

print(f"sequential: {sequential_time:.2f}s for {N_CHAINS} chains")
print(f"parallel:   {parallel_time:.2f}s for {N_CHAINS} chains")
print(f"speedup:    {sequential_time / parallel_time:.1f}x")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.figure(figsize=(5, 4))
plt.bar(["sequential", "parallel"], [sequential_time, parallel_time], color=["tab:gray", "tab:blue"])
plt.ylabel("wall-clock seconds")
plt.title(f"{N_CHAINS} chains, sequential vs Worker-parallel")
plt.show()

# Sanity check: parallelizing changes nothing about what's being computed --
# each chain is independent either way, just with a different seed.
beta0_name = [n for n in sequential_fits[0].param_names if n.startswith("beta")][0]
seq_means = [f[beta0_name].mean() for f in sequential_fits]
par_means = [f[beta0_name].mean() for f in parallel_fits]
print("sequential beta[0] means:", [round(m, 3) for m in seq_means])
print("parallel   beta[0] means:", [round(m, 3) for m in par_means])
```
